translationRepairs: Because Lingkun had risen to prominence, Emperor Shizong promoted Lun to acting military commissioner of Chenzhou; when Lingkun assumed command of Chenzhou, Lun was transferred to Xuzhou.
Because Lingkun had risen to prominence, Emperor Shizong promoted Lun to army administrator of Chenzhou; when Lingkun assumed command of Chenzhou, Lun was transferred to Xu prefecture.

The Chinese promotes Lun to 陳州行軍司馬, the army-administrative Sima of Chenzhou, not an acting military commissioner; 徙倫許州 then moves him to Xu prefecture, which is distinct from 徐州 in the preceding sentence.
Emperor Shizong, because Lingkun was eminent, promoted [Lun] to acting military commissioner of Chenzhou; when Lingkun took command of Chenzhou, [Lun] was transferred to Xuzhou.
Emperor Shizong, because Lingkun was eminent, promoted [Lun] to army administrator of Chenzhou; when Lingkun took command of Chenzhou, [Lun] was transferred to Xu prefecture.
The same two errors appear in the literal line: 行軍司馬 is not an acting military commissioner, and 許州 is Xu prefecture, not 徐州.
Lingkun joined the future Song founder and Li Chongjin in a combined attack and routed the Wu forces.
Lingkun joined Xuanzu and Li Chongjin in a combined attack and routed the Wu forces.
The named colleague is 宣祖, the temple name Xuanzu; the Chinese does not identify him as the future Song founder, a role reserved for 太祖 elsewhere.
Lingkun, together with the future founder, Li Chongjin, and others, combined forces and struck them, inflicting a great defeat on the Wu.
Lingkun, together with Xuanzu and Li Chongjin, combined forces and struck them, inflicting a great defeat on the Wu.
宣祖 is Xuanzu, not the future founder, but the proposed literal still invents “and others”; the Chinese names only Lingkun, Xuanzu, and Li Chongjin.
When Emperor Shizong led the campaign in person and learned that Yangzhou was undefended, he dispatched Lingkun along with the future founder, Bai Yan'yu, Zhao Chao, and others to seize it.
When Emperor Shizong led the campaign in person and learned that Yangzhou was undefended, he dispatched Lingkun along with Xuanzu, Bai Yan'yu, Zhao Chao, and others to seize it.
The dispatched colleague is again 宣祖 (Xuanzu), listed with Bai Yan'yu and Zhao Chao; the Chinese does not call him the future founder.
Emperor Shizong personally led the campaign; hearing that Yangzhou was undefended, he sent Lingkun together with the future founder, Bai Yan'yu, Zhao Chao, and others to raid it.
Emperor Shizong personally led the campaign; hearing that Yangzhou was undefended, he sent Lingkun together with Xuanzu, Bai Yan'yu, Zhao Chao, and others to raid it.
The literal line repeats the 宣祖 / future-founder mismatch; Xuanzu is the name in the Chinese.
On returning to court he was granted the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and made military governor of Zhen'an Circuit.
On returning to court he was granted the honorary title of acting Grand Commandant and made military governor of Zhen'an Circuit.
檢校太尉 is the honorary/acting Grand Commandant (太尉), not Grand Preceptor (太師).
Upon returning to court, [Lingkun] was granted the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment and made military governor of Zhen'an Circuit.
Upon returning to court, [Lingkun] was granted the additional title of acting Grand Commandant by special appointment and made military governor of Zhen'an Circuit.
The literal line likewise renders 檢校太尉 as Grand Preceptor; acting Grand Commandant matches 太尉.
At the founding of Song he was transferred to Tiansping Circuit, appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard, and made a co-director of the Chancellery.
At the founding of Song he was transferred to Tianping Circuit, appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard, and made a co-director of the Chancellery.
天平軍 is Tianping; Tiansping is a misspelling of the circuit name.
At the beginning of Song, he was transferred to Tiansping Circuit, appointed commander-in-chief of the palace horse-and-foot guard corps, and made co-director of the Chancellery.
At the beginning of Song, he was transferred to Tianping Circuit, appointed commander-in-chief of the palace horse-and-foot guard corps, and made co-director of the Chancellery.
The literal line repeats the misspelling Tiansping for 天平軍.
After the rebellion was suppressed he was additionally made chief minister and ordered to return to Cazhou.
After the rebellion was suppressed he was additionally made chief minister and ordered to return to Chanzhou.
詔還澶州 sends him back to Chanzhou; Cazhou misreads 澶.
When [the rebellion] was pacified, he was additionally made chief minister by special appointment and ordered to return to Cazhou.
When [the rebellion] was pacified, he was additionally made chief minister by special appointment and ordered to return to Chanzhou.
The literal line copies Cazhou for 澶州; Chanzhou is the correct reading.
After Jing and Xiang were pacified he was granted the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
After Jing and Xiang were pacified he was granted the honorary title of Grand Marshal.
檢校太尉 is an honorary Grand Marshal/Commandant, not Grand Preceptor; the proposed Grand Marshal matches 太尉 and the chapter’s own rendering at s0252.
Once Jing and Xiang were pacified, he was granted the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment.
Once Jing and Xiang were pacified, he was granted the additional title of Grand Marshal by special appointment.
The literal line mistranslates 太尉 as Grand Preceptor; Grand Marshal is accurate.
Shortly afterward he took charge as prefect of Weizhou.
Shortly afterward he took charge as prefect of Yuizhou.
俄領蔚州刺史 makes him prefect of Yuizhou (蔚州); Weizhou would be 衛州.
Shortly afterward he took charge as prefect of Weizhou.
Shortly afterward he took charge as prefect of Yuizhou.
The literal line likewise reads 蔚州 as Weizhou; Yuizhou is the prefecture named in the Chinese.
He was made commander of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, then shortly afterward also commanded the Right Feathered Forest, and was transferred to hold Yan-Yan Circuit.
He was made commander of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, then shortly afterward also commanded the Right Feathered Forest, and was transferred to hold Fuyan Circuit.
改鎮鄜延 transfers him to Fuyan Circuit; Yan-Yan drops 鄜 and doubles 延.
He was changed to commander of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, then shortly concurrently commanded the Right Feathered Forest as well, and was transferred to hold Yan-Yan Circuit.
He was changed to commander of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, then shortly concurrently commanded the Right Feathered Forest as well, and was transferred to hold Fuyan Circuit.
The literal line repeats Yan-Yan Circuit for 鄜延; Fuyan is the established reading.
When the Liao invaders came south, an edict ordered Yanqing to lead his troops to resist them at Cazhou.
When the Liao invaders came south, an edict ordered Yanqing to lead his troops to resist them at Chanzhou.
拒戰澶州 is resistance at Chanzhou; Cazhou is the same misreading of 澶 as in s0054.
When the Liao invaders came south, an edict ordered Yanqing to lead his troops to resist them at Cazhou.
When the Liao invaders came south, an edict ordered Yanqing to lead his troops to resist them at Chanzhou.
The literal line copies Cazhou for 澶州.
He also served under Li Shouzhen in suppressing Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou, was transferred to hold Xuzhou, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
He also served under Li Shouzhen in suppressing Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou, was transferred to hold Xu Prefecture, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
移鎮許州 is a transfer to Xu prefecture, not 徐州 (Xuzhou), so the original conflates two different places.
When Du Chongwei surrendered the main army at the Hutuo River, urgent orders summoned Yanqing and Gao Xingzhou to lead palace troops to encamp at Canyuan.
When Du Chongwei surrendered the main army at the Hutuo River, urgent orders summoned Yanqing and Gao Xingzhou to lead palace troops to encamp at Chanyuan.
屯澶淵 is an encampment at Chanyuan; Canyuan misreads 澶.
When Du Chongwei surrendered the main army at the Hutuo River, urgent orders summoned Yanqing and Gao Xingzhou to lead palace troops to encamp at Canyuan.
When Du Chongwei surrendered the main army at the Hutuo River, urgent orders summoned Yanqing and Gao Xingzhou to lead palace troops to encamp at Chanyuan.
The literal line repeats Canyuan for 澶淵.
During the Qianyou era he was additionally made director of the Chancellery, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, appointed honorary grand preceptor, and transferred to hold Qingzhou.
During the Qianyou era he was additionally made director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, appointed honorary Grand Guardian, and transferred to hold Qingzhou.
中書令 is Director of the Secretariat, not the Chancellery (侍中), but the proposed sentence still renders 守太保 as honorary grand preceptor; 太保 is Grand Guardian, not 太師.
During Qianyou he was additionally made director of the Chancellery, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, appointed honorary grand preceptor, and transferred to hold Qingzhou.
During Qianyou he was additionally made director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, appointed honorary Grand Guardian, and transferred to hold Qingzhou.
The Secretariat correction is right, but 守太保 remains mistranslated as honorary grand preceptor in the proposed literal line.
When Yang Ye and his associates were killed, Yanqing was urgently summoned to the capital.
When Yang Bin and his associates were killed, Yanqing was urgently summoned to the capital.
及殺楊邠輩 names Yang Bin (楊邠); Yang Ye would be 楊業.
When Yang Ye and his associates were killed, [Yanqing] was urgently summoned to the capital.
When Yang Bin and his associates were killed, [Yanqing] was urgently summoned to the capital.
The literal line repeats Yang Ye for 楊邠; Yang Bin is the name in the Chinese.
He was soon transferred to hold Yanzhou.
He was soon transferred to hold Yunzhou.
俄移鎮鄆州 transfers him to Yunzhou; Yanzhou is 兗州, already used in the preceding campaign sentence.
Soon he was transferred to hold Yanzhou.
Soon he was transferred to hold Yunzhou.
The literal line copies Yanzhou for 鄆州.
When Prince Wang Yin of Wei prefecture was summoned, the court intended to have Yanqing replace him in his post.
When Wang Yin of Wei prefecture was summoned, the court intended to have Yanqing replace him in his post.
會召魏府王殷 names Wang Yin; 王 is his surname, not the title Prince.
When Prince Wang Yin of Wei prefecture was summoned, [the court] intended to have Yanqing replace him in his post.
When Wang Yin of Wei prefecture was summoned, [the court] intended to have Yanqing replace him in his post.
The literal line likewise turns the surname 王 into Prince.
After Emperor Shaodi of Jin fell to the Khitan, Empress Dowager Deguang asked those around her, "Where is Yanqing?"
After Emperor Shaodi of Jin fell to the Khitan, Deguang's mother asked those around her, "Where is Yanqing?"
德光之母 is Deguang’s mother, not an empress named Deguang or an empress-dowager title of Deguang himself.
After Emperor Shaodi of Jin fell to the Khitan, Empress Dowager of Deguang asked those around her: "Where is Yanqing?"
After Emperor Shaodi of Jin fell to the Khitan, Deguang's mother asked those around her: "Where is Yanqing?"
The literal “Empress Dowager of Deguang” misreads 德光之母 as a title of Deguang; the speaker is his mother.
Empress Dowager Deguang said, "To leave this man in central China — what a blunder!"
Deguang's mother said, "To leave this man in central China — what a blunder!"
德光母 continues 德光之母 from the previous sentence; the speaker is Deguang’s mother, not Empress Dowager Deguang.
The empress dowager of Deguang said: "To leave this man in central China — how great a blunder!"
Deguang's mother said: "To leave this man in central China — how great a blunder!"
The literal line again attaches an empress-dowager title to Deguang; 德光母 is his mother.
When the army returned, he was formally appointed prefect of Caizhou and put in charge of Bing and Cao prefectures.
When the army returned, he was formally appointed prefect of Caizhou and put in charge of Bing and Chan prefectures.
知幷澶二州 is charge of Bing and Chan prefectures; 澶 is Chan (Chanzhou), not Cao.
When the army returned, he was formally appointed prefect of Caizhou and put in charge of Bing and Cao prefectures.
When the army returned, he was formally appointed prefect of Caizhou and put in charge of Bing and Chan prefectures.
The literal line copies Cao for 澶 in 幷澶二州.
